sources.authority: Environment Agency / Defra Data Services Platform
facts: timestamped DTM surveys have been collected across England since 1998
downloads are GeoTIFF rasters in 5km zip files
elevations are in metres referenced to Ordnance Survey Newlyn
data is aligned to the OS Grid
all LIDAR data has vertical accuracy of plus or minus 15cm RMSE
the transformation used is specific to the survey time period

sources.authority: Environment Agency / Defra Data Services Platform
facts: time-stamped point cloud is available for surveys going back to 2006
DTM and DSM rasters are derived from point-cloud data
historic archiving means a matching point cloud may not exist for every surface model
point returns are classified into ground and surface objects
manual DTM editing means classified ground points do not necessarily match final DTM
point cloud downloads are yearly 5km LAZ tiles aligned to the OS Grid

sources.authority: Environment Agency / Defra Data Services Platform
facts: ground-truth points are independently surveyed on flat unambiguous surfaces
each ground-truth point has plus or minus 3cm RMSE accuracy
timestamped LIDAR must report less than plus or minus 15cm RMSE to pass quality control
standard deviation and random error must be less than 10cm
ground-truth surveys may be reused when under 5 years old, or under 3 years for coastal projects

promotion_rule: Parcel height difference may use timestamped DTM only with survey-period transform, vertical datum and QC lineage; raw ground-class points are not substituted for the manually edited final DTM.
